title: A self-hosted resume tailor that refuses to invent your experience
summary: A self-hosted resume tailor that will not invent your experience. Dossier drafts only from your profile, shows missing skills as gaps, and its daily job agent never sends or applies: https://github.com/AienTech/dossier
body_markdown:
One failure you do not want from an AI resume writer is a confident line about experience you do not have, which you then have to defend in an interview. Dossier, a self-hosted job search app from AienTech/dossier, lists avoiding that among its features. Its tailored resumes and cover letters use only facts from your profile. When a posting asks for something your profile does not have, Dossier shows it as a gap and does not make it up.

Every resume and cover letter in the app comes from that one profile.

## One profile, many tailored drafts

The profile is detailed: experience, volunteering, projects, education, certifications with issuer, dates, credential ID and a verify link, publications cited in your own style, and references. You can start it from an existing resume in PDF, Word or Markdown. A strength meter counts only what a profile needs.

For each job you paste a posting. Dossier pulls out the details and requirements, matches them against your profile, and writes a tailored resume and cover letter in the tone you pick. You refine them in a chat, edit or regenerate any part, undo AI changes or roll back to an earlier version, and download PDFs. Twelve resume themes and a theme builder handle the look. A board and a table track every application from draft to offer, and a dashboard shows your funnel over 30 days, 90 days or all time.

Finding postings is built in too. It searches JSearch (which covers LinkedIn, Indeed and more), Adzuna or FreeHire, and it lists hiring startups from YC job posts and the Hacker News "Who is hiring?" thread. The project says it reads the startups' sites politely and follows their robots.txt.

## Where the agent stops

The optional job agent is where I looked hardest, since it runs on its own every day. You save up to three named searches. Once a day the enabled ones run in order, skip what you have seen, score new postings against your profile, and keep the best on an Agent screen with its reasons. All searches share a budget of three first-page source requests per rolling 24 hours, and failed attempts count. It can prepare tailored drafts, which wait for your review. It never sends or applies.

The same line holds across the integrations. The MCP connector lets Claude search jobs, score them, read your profile and save a resume as a Draft, and it never sends or deletes anything. The Gmail and Calendar connection can send an application from your own address and draft replies to employers, but nothing goes out without your confirmation.

## Where your data goes

Dossier is for one person on a small server, with one password and your data in your own PostgreSQL database or a single SQLite file. The privacy picture depends on the model you choose. A local model through Ollama or LM Studio keeps your profile and documents on your own hardware. A hosted model, any OpenAI-compatible API, Anthropic or Mistral, receives the profile facts it drafts from, so pick accordingly. You can also export and import everything as one file, keep nightly backups, or use Delete everything.

## Running it locally

You need Docker and about 2 GB of free memory. Fetch the Compose file, generate the secrets, and hash a password:

```bash
mkdir ~/dossier && cd ~/dossier
curl -fsSL -o compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AienTech/dossier/main/compose.production.yml
echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)" > .env
echo "DOSSIER_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)" >> .env
docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/aientech/dossier hash-password
```

Add the printed `argon2id:` line to `.env` as `DOSSIER_PASSWORD`, then run `docker compose up -d`. The first start pulls an image of about 1.7 GB. Open localhost:3000 and pick a model under Settings, AI provider. A desktop app for Windows and Linux skips Docker entirely. I would paste one posting you have already applied to and check the gap list against what you know is missing.
